Package io.mavlink4j.transport

package io.mavlink4j.transport
L1 — bytes in, bytes out over a MavlinkLink (UDP listen/target, TCP client, serial). Knows nothing about frames. May depend on L0 only.

Layer rule: a package never reaches two levels down; see docs/architecture.md.

    LinkPeer

    MavlinkLink
    Bytes in, bytes out.
    SerialChannel
    The byte-level seam SerialLink polls/writes through.
    SerialLink
    A serial (jSerialComm-backed) MavlinkLink — modelled line-for-line on TcpClientLink: SerialLink.preservesMessageBoundaries() is honestly false (one SerialLink.poll(java.time.Duration) may return less than one frame, more than one, or a frame split across several polls, exactly like a TCP stream), id is stable for the port's whole life ("serial:" + portDescriptor), and SerialLink.send(byte[], int, int, io.mavlink4j.transport.LinkPeer)'s target parameter is accepted for interface uniformity only — a serial wire has exactly one destination, the far end of the cable, which SerialLink.defaultTarget() honestly reports as LinkPeer.NONE (a serial link has no addressable network peer at all, unlike UDP/TCP).
    TcpClientLink
    Dials out to a fixed remote host:port over TCP.
    UdpListenLink
    Listens — binds a local UDP address and accepts datagrams from whoever sends to it.
    UdpTargetLink
    Dials a fixed destination from an ephemeral local UDP port — the shape a TX simulator needs (send a synthetic feed at one configured address).
